question.problem: Find the vertex of the elliptic paraboloid $z-5=3(x-2)^{2}+2(y+1)^{2}.$
question.worked_solution:
The general equation of an elliptic paraboloid oriented along the $z$-axis with vertex at a point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ is 

$$
z-{z}_{0}=\frac{(x-{x}_{0})^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-{y}_{0})^{2}}{{b}^{2}}.
$$

To find the vertex, we rewrite our equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}z-5 & =3(x-2)^{2}+2(y+1)^{2} \\ z-5 & =\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{1/3}+\frac{(y+1)^{2}}{1/2} \\ z-5 & =\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{1/3}+\frac{(y-(-1))^{2}}{1/2}\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us the equation of an elliptic paraboloid that has its vertex at $(2,-1,5).$
